titleZh: Valley新技术革新中心支轴灌溉管理
summaryZh: Valley Irrigation推出基于电力线通信的机器诊断系统和统一软件平台AgSense 365，帮助农民实时监测中心支轴灌溉系统各塔架状态，精准定位故障，减少非计划停机，并通过变量灌溉和远程管理实现节水增产。文章还展望了AI驱动的预测性维护和智能灌溉决策前景。
featuredReason: 中心支轴灌溉是大田作物水肥管理的核心环节，Valley将电力线通信诊断、统一平台和AI预测维护结合，展示了从硬件传感→数据平台→智能决策的完整路径，对智慧农业和畜牧配套饲草料基地的灌溉管理有直接参考价值。

Valley’s new tech revolutionizes center-pivot management

Diagnostic features and a unified software platform help farmers maximize uptime, conserve water and make data-driven irrigation decisions.

Andy Castillo,Editor of Farm Equipment and Machinery,Farm ProgressOctober 31, 2026

schedule4 Min Read

New tech from Valley Irrigation allows farmers to monitor their center-pivot systems and pinpoint issues. Curt Arens

link

Subscribe to Farm Progress AGTech — our free, twice-weekly newsletter delivering the latest innovations, emerging technologies and expert insights to your inbox.

Every good farmer knows that time is money. Maximizing profit means identifying bottlenecks and streamlining efficiency. Center-pivot management is one friction point in many operations. Valley Irrigation aims to streamline it with technology.

“Our ultimate goal is improving machine uptime by reducing unplanned machine downtime. We don’t want our machines to be stopping in the middle of a high irrigation need-demand time of the year, potentially causing crop-related stress,” said Troy Long, vice president of product hardware and warranty at Valley Irrigation.

To do that, Valley’s machine diagnostics relies on power line communications technology that links hardware embedded in each tower box to a primary Icon control panel, via touchscreen and remote control. This lets farmers monitor each tower’s position relative to the rest of the machine and pinpoint issue areas. The system sends an alert when trouble arises, pinpointing precise issue areas to make diagnostics easier.

Related:Harvest memories: Antique combines and corn pickers

“Once you’re at the tower that has a problem, it’s pretty easy to see, ‘this thing is getting stuck,’ or ‘one of the tires or the gearbox appears to be failing,’ ” Long said, noting its capabilities encompass tire pressure, tower runtime monitoring, alignment detection and water pressure tracking across the entire span.

“Historically, when pivots end up having an issue like I described, it opens a safety circuit. You just get a fault,” he said. “That safety fault could mean all kinds of things. So, a person has to go to the field and look. You are blind as to where to go to look for a problem.”

The future of irrigation

Valley aims to take its diagnostics capability one step further by being able to schedule optimal service timing and predict near-term catastrophes before they happen.

Recent advancements in software are driving that long term vision. Last year, the brand consolidated several legacy platforms — Valley 365, AgSense, PivoTrac and others — into a single ecosystem called AgSense 365. The unified approach lets farmers monitor their pivot devices and track irrigation practices from a single interface.

“AgSense 365 is the culmination of all of these separate platforms that we had at one point in time, bringing all of the best capabilities and features into the single ecosystem,” said Ashley Anderson, assistant general manager for the AgSense business.

Related:T-L's new touch panel boosts management of linear sprinklers

The need for a unified platform “came to light because of grower feedback,” she said. “It was predominantly vocalized, ‘I want one app, one place, one-stop shop to go to perform all of my activities.’ ”

Looking to the future, Anderson said more capabilities are on the horizon, including artificial intelligence-based programs that can help farmers extract and leverage their in-field data to make more informed irrigation decisions. The foundational telematic software now embedded within Valley pivots will enable that evolution.

“Most of the features that we’ve added here in the last year or so have been to improve and enhance the usability of the product set, so that you have a common experience between what you’re doing in the field and what you’re doing remotely through the application, and then giving you enhanced data and more information to help make meaningful decisions,” Anderson said.

Meeting today’s challenges

There are other challenges besides labor optimization that Valley seeks to resolve. Water shortage is increasingly an issue for farmers working in drought-stricken areas, and those experiencing rapid aquifer decline. Crops don’t differentiate between water delivery, making financial payback for those in declining water areas difficult.

Related:Claas invests $10M in Nebraska research center

Long said precision irrigation technology could help farmers produce more yield with less water by more efficiently targeting optimal growth stages — a particular benefit when paired with practices like fertigation.

“We have done quite a significant amount of work with our [variable-rate irrigation] solutions on the software side over the last couple of years to help improve the usability and simplification of the use of VRI, because it can be quite a complex process, especially when you get into individual sprinklers, defining zones and then the application,” Anderson said.

Valley’s approach to the challenges that today’s farmers face — from labor availability to water shortages — is holistic, focusing on hardware efficiency, sensing technology, software intelligence, remote management and predictive analytics.

Anderson described anticipated future advancements as a “hockey stick” — rapidly increasing exponentially.

“We’re trying to simplify through technology. Then, who knows? With AI, we couldn’t have predicted where it is even a year ago, let alone where it’s going to go. We’re trying to use every bit of that type of technology to put the information more easily in the hands of our users to be more effective with the product,” Long said.

About the Author

Andy Castillo

Editor of Farm Equipment and Machinery, Farm Progress

Andy Castillo started his career in journalism about a decade ago as a television news cameraperson and producer before transitioning to a regional newspaper covering western Massachusetts, where he wrote about local farming. Between military deployments with the Air Force and covering the news, he earned an MFA in creative nonfiction writing from Bay Path University, building on the English degree he earned from the University of Massachusetts Amherst. In his role at Farm Progress, Castillo covers agricultural technology, new machinery and the constantly evolving farm equipment marketplace.

Castillo splits his time between the open road and western Massachusetts with his wife, Brianna, a travel nurse who specializes in pediatric oncology, and their rescue pup, Rio. When not attending farm shows, Castillo enjoys playing music, snowboarding, writing, cooking and restoring their 1920 craftsman bungalow. You can find Castillo at farm machinery shows across the country.

translationZh:
每个好农民都知道时间就是金钱。最大化利润意味着识别瓶颈并简化效率。中心支轴灌溉管理是许多运营中的一个摩擦点。Valley Irrigation旨在通过技术来简化它。

“我们的最终目标是提高机器正常运行时间，减少非计划停机。我们不希望机器在一年中高灌溉需求时期停止运行，这可能导致作物应激，”Valley Irrigation产品硬件和保修副总裁Troy Long说。

为此，Valley的机器诊断依赖于电力线通信技术，将每个塔架箱中嵌入的硬件通过触摸屏和远程控制连接到主Icon控制面板。这使农民能够监测每个塔架相对于机器其余部分的位置，并精确定位问题区域。系统在出现故障时发送警报，精确定位具体问题区域，使诊断更容易。

“一旦你到达有问题的塔架，就很容易看出‘这东西卡住了’或‘其中一个轮胎或变速箱似乎要坏了’，”Long说，并指出其能力涵盖整个跨度的轮胎压力、塔架运行时间监测、对齐检测和水压跟踪。

“历史上，当支轴出现我描述的问题时，它会打开安全电路。你只会得到一个故障，”他说。“那个安全故障可能意味着各种情况。所以，一个人必须去田里查看。你根本不知道去哪里找问题。”

**灌溉的未来**

Valley旨在通过能够安排最佳服务时间和在灾难发生前预测近期灾难，将其诊断能力提升一步。

软件的最新进展正在推动这一长期愿景。去年，该品牌将几个传统平台——Valley 365、AgSense、PivoTrac等——整合到一个名为AgSense 365的单一生态系统中。统一的方法让农民可以从单一界面监测支轴设备并跟踪灌溉实践。

“AgSense 365是我们曾经拥有的所有这些独立平台的结晶，将所有最佳能力和功能整合到一个生态系统中，”AgSense业务助理总经理Ashley Anderson说。

统一平台的需求“因种植者反馈而显现，”她说。“主要是明确表达，‘我想要一个应用、一个地方、一站式商店来执行我所有的活动。’”

展望未来，Anderson表示更多能力即将到来，包括基于人工智能的程序，可以帮助农民提取和利用田间数据做出更明智的灌溉决策。现在嵌入Valley支轴中的基础远程信息处理软件将实现这一演变。

“我们在过去一年左右添加的大多数功能都是为了提高和增强产品集的可用性，以便你在田间所做的和通过应用程序远程所做的之间有共同的体验，然后为你提供增强的数据和更多信息，帮助做出有意义的决策，”Anderson说。

**应对当今挑战**

除了劳动力优化，Valley还寻求解决其他挑战。水资源短缺日益成为在干旱地区和经历含水层快速下降的农民的问题。作物不区分水输送，使得在缺水地区财务回报困难。

Long说，精准灌溉技术可以通过更有效地针对最佳生长阶段，帮助农民用更少的水生产更多产量——与施肥灌溉等实践配合时尤其有益。

“过去几年，我们在软件方面对变量灌溉解决方案做了大量工作，以帮助提高VRI使用的可用性和简化性，因为它可能是一个相当复杂的过程，特别是当你涉及单个喷头、定义区域然后应用时，”Anderson说。

Valley应对当今农民面临的挑战——从劳动力可用性到水资源短缺——的方法是整体的，专注于硬件效率、传感技术、软件智能、远程管理和预测分析。

Anderson将预期的未来进步描述为“曲棍球棒”——快速指数级增长。

“我们试图通过技术来简化。然后，谁知道呢？有了AI，我们一年前都无法预测它现在在哪里，更不用说它将走向何方。我们正在尝试利用每一种这类技术，将信息更容易地交到用户手中，使产品更有效，”Long说。
contentHtml: Diagnostic features and a unified software platform help farmers maximize uptime, conserve water and make data-driven irrigation decisions.
